explanation: The E138A mutation causes resistance through an indirect allosteric mechanism despite being located ~43 Å from the NNRTI-binding pocket. Glutamate's negative charge at position 138 stabilizes the palm domain architecture through electrostatic interactions with positively charged residues; its replacement with alanine removes this charge anchor, destabilizing the precise conformational geometry required for optimal etravirine binding and positioning of key contact residues. The 50 Ų decrease in local volume combined with loss of the charged side chain likely permits subtle shifts in palm domain flexibility that collectively weaken the multivalent interactions etravirine makes within the NNRTI pocket, explaining the modest but measurable reduction in binding affinity.
